name: Nintendo 2001
look: Y2K console chrome — brushed periwinkle bevels, carbon-navy command bars, chamfered plates, rationed warm signal colour.

hero.title:
POLYGON 64
CHANGES EVERYTHING
hero.sub: Sixty-four bits of processing power. Four controller ports. Nine launch titles. The next generation is not coming — it is plugged in.

features.title: INSIDE THE MACHINE
features.sub: Every component chosen for one thing: frames on the screen.

items.title: 64-BIT PROCESSOR
items.body: 93.75 MHz of custom silicon, co-designed with the graphics unit so the two never wait on each other.

items.title: REALITY ENGINE
items.body: Hardware texture filtering, mip-mapping and anti-aliasing — in the box, not as an add-on.

items.title: FOUR PORTS
items.body: Four controllers plug straight in. No adapter, no multi-tap, no arguments about whose turn it is.

items.title: CARTRIDGE LOADING
items.body: No load times. Blow on the cartridge, push it in, and you are playing inside four seconds.

items.title: RUMBLE PAK
items.body: Force feedback in the controller grip, driven by the game rather than bolted on afterwards.

items.title: EXPANSION BAY
items.body: A memory expansion doubles the working RAM and unlocks high-resolution mode on supported titles.

showcases.title: NINE TITLES AT LAUNCH
showcases.body: Four first-party games and five from partner studios, all shipping on day one. Three more arrive before the holidays, including the racing title that has been in the magazines all year.

showcases.title: BUILT TO SURVIVE A CHILDHOOD
showcases.body: Drop-tested from a metre onto carpet and concrete. Reinforced port housings, a cartridge slot rated to ten thousand insertions, and a shell moulded in one piece.

gallery.title: GAME LIBRARY
gallery.sub: Nine at launch. Twelve by December. Browse the full catalogue.

testimonial.quote: I saved for eleven months and queued from six in the morning. Nineteen years later it is still under the television, and it still works.
testimonial.name: Danny Kolar

pricing.title: GET YOURS
pricing.sub: Three bundles. All include the console, one controller and the power supply.

tiers.name: CONSOLE
tiers.desc: The system, one controller, and the cables.

tiers.name: STARTER SET
tiers.desc: The system plus a launch title and a memory card.

tiers.name: COLLECTOR
tiers.desc: Two controllers, three games, expansion bay module.

items.a: The console, one controller, an AV cable, the power supply and the printed manual. Memory cards and additional controllers are sold separately.
No. The Polygon 64 uses a new cartridge format with a different pin count and a physically different slot, so previous-generation games will not fit.
Four, out of the box, with four ports on the front of the console. No adapter is required, though not every title supports four players.

items.q: What does the expansion bay do?
items.a: The memory expansion module doubles the working RAM and enables a high-resolution display mode on titles that support it. It is included in the Collector bundle.

cta.title: PLAY IT ON POLYGON 64
cta.sub: Available now at retailers everywhere. Register your system for a free game voucher.

footer.tagline: Play it loud. Play it on Polygon 64.

notes: Every region is a bevelled metal plate: a light top edge, a chrome-indigo shadow line below. The page is assembled from panels rather than laid out on a grid.
Chamfered (cut-corner) geometry on the largest modules; most chrome is sharp-edged, with rounding reserved for the logo pill and circular badges.
A carbon-navy command layer with halftone texture carries the top nav, the right rail and the footer.
Warmth is rationed as directional signal only — gold for menu words, amber for utility chips, orange for every forward or submit cue.
Density is the point. Minimal whitespace, packed modular panels, and a hero field tinted per section.
